description.plain:
Card 1 – Business Questions & Audience

Business problem

Manufacturing operations must balance production output, yield, scrap, rework and product quality. When production confirmations, goods movements, inspection results and quality notifications are analysed separately, managers may struggle to understand where losses occur and which plant, shift, work centre, supplier lot or batch requires attention.

Business objectives

Monitor production quantity and confirmed yield performance across plants.

Measure confirmed scrap and rework to highlight potential production losses.

Relate quality defect information to suppliers, vendor lots, batches and production context where source linkage is available.

Reconcile confirmation-based quantities with material movement quantities without double counting.

Provide drill-down analysis to support investigation and operational follow-up.

Target audience and decisions

Persona — Questions they need answered — Decision supported

CFO — Where are material losses and production inefficiencies concentrated? — Prioritize financial and operational review.

Plant Head — Which plant is below its yield or scrap expectations? — Assign plant-level investigation and improvement actions.

Production Manager — Which work centre or shift is associated with lower yield or higher scrap? — Review process settings, schedules and execution.

Quality Manager — Which defect causes, batches or inspection outcomes need attention? — Initiate quality investigation and disposition review.

Supply Chain Manager — Which supplier or vendor lot shows a quality impact? — Review supplier performance and incoming material controls.

Three key business questions

Which plants are performing well or poorly in terms of production yield and scrap?

Which suppliers, batches, shifts and work centres contribute to quality defects and production losses?

How can production quantities and material movements be reconciled to improve traceability?

Current-state challenge

Information can be distributed across PP, MM and QM processes. Different transaction grains and quantity definitions can lead to inconsistent comparisons if the data is combined without controlled relationships and agreed KPI definitions.

description.plain:
Card 6 – Insights & ROI

Dashboard observations

Area — Value shown in dashboard — Interpretation

Production — 48.7 lakh kg production order quantity. — Overall order quantity in the current dashboard context.

Yield — 93.2% confirmed yield performance. — A measure of confirmed output relative to the stated production quantity, subject to formula validation.

Scrap — 4.59% confirmed scrap performance. — Highlights the share of confirmed scrap in the defined production denominator.

Rework — 2.25% confirmed rework performance. — Shows the level of confirmed rework requiring monitoring.

Quality — 2.14 lakh total quality defect impact. — Signals quality-related impact; calculation and unit should be confirmed.

ROI measurement framework

Value driver — Baseline to capture — After implementation measure

Reporting productivity — Time spent preparing manual reports and consolidating data. — Time to access standard dashboard views; hours saved per reporting cycle.

Investigation speed — Average time from identifying an issue to locating relevant plant/order/batch details. — Time to isolate relevant records using filters and drill-down.

Yield improvement — Baseline yield by plant/material/product over an agreed period. — Change in yield using the same definition and comparable production mix.

Scrap reduction — Baseline scrap quantity and scrap cost for a comparable period. — Change in scrap quantity/cost after corrective actions.

Rework reduction — Baseline rework quantity and associated cost. — Change in rework quantity/cost after process improvements.

Supplier quality — Baseline supplier / vendor-lot defect trend. — Change in incoming quality issues and repeat supplier occurrences.

ROI calculation approach

Annual measurable benefit = reporting hours saved × loaded hourly cost + verified scrap cost reduction + verified rework cost reduction + other approved measurable benefits.

ROI (%) = (Annual measurable benefit − annual solution operating cost) ÷ annual solution operating cost × 100.

Implementation Considerations & Acceptance Criteria

Area — Acceptance check

KPI correctness — Business owner signs off formula, unit, denominator, aggregation and target.

Reconciliation — Production confirmation and goods movement totals are separately reconciled to agreed SAP reports.

Traceability — Sample orders and batches can be followed through the approved source relationships.

No double counting — Fact totals remain stable when dimensions or related facts are added to analysis.

Filters — Plant, date, material, batch and other controls return expected results.

Performance — Story loads within the agreed performance expectation for representative data volumes.

Access — Users see only the data authorized by their roles and organizational scope.

Refresh — Refresh schedule, monitoring and failure notification are agreed and tested.
